insight.title: How Light Paints the World
insight.subtitle: The quiet dialogue between the sun and our eyes.

sections.text: Every morning, the world emerges from a deep, velvet shadow. We wake to a room filled with color, yet color does not live inside the objects themselves. Instead, it is a fleeting gift from the sun. Without the gentle touch of traveling beams, the red apple and the blue sea are exactly the same.

Science tells us that light travels in tiny, silent waves. When these waves strike a surface, the object keeps some for itself and reflects others back to us. Your eyes catch these wandering rays, turning them into a signal. In that instant, your mind builds a vibrant map of the space around you.

This means you never truly touch the world with your hands alone. You perceive it through a constant, shimmering rain of energy. It is a reminder that we are deeply connected to the stars. We are not just observers of the light; we are the very place where the universe finally sees itself.

news.title: As war in Middle East escalates, PM Shehbaz departs on brief visit to Saudi Arabia
news.description: PMO says premier to discuss "regional security situation and bilateral relations" with Saudi crown prince; FO says visit part of Pakistan's efforts for de-escalation.

news.title: Maxx Crosby commits after nixed trade to Ravens: I'm a Raider
news.description: Maxx Crosby made his first public comments since the Ravens backed out of a trade that would've sent him to Baltimore, writing on X on Wednesday night, "Im a Raider. I'm back."

news.title: Oil price surges back to about $100 as explosions reported on two more foreign ships in Gulf
news.description: Iranian attacks on ships intensify after major countries agree to tap unprecedented emergency reserves to cushion the blow of war.

news.title: Iran leader calls for Hormuz closure as oil price spikes
news.description: In his first public statement, supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said Iran should use choking off Hormuz as leverage, while the IEA says the conflict is unleashing the largest oil supply disruption in history. Follow DW.

news.title: War and oil price at $200 a barrel could force Australia to inflation
news.description: Economists are predicting two more rate rises in the next eight weeks. But with oil prices climbing, it could also mean an Australian recession.
